result.summary:
Re-gate limited to the rework (commit 2dadd9f, at HEAD 2dadd9f on feature/WF02-REQ-019) that closes my prior FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-01b-design-validator.json): docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md SS4.6's three callback handlers did not state a derive-then-gate discipline before their write, leaving AC3/security-invariants.md S1's 'no write to profiles before consent' guarantee unproven for a forged/stale callback. Not a full re-run of every check against the whole design (already PASSed everything else in the prior gate); scoped to what changed since, per the handoff's own instructions, plus a full re-confirmation that nothing else regressed.

1. Read `git show 2dadd9f -- docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md` myself in full (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary in handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-01-code-designer-rework1.json). Confirmed `git diff 0416a91 2dadd9f --name-only` touches exactly docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md plus the two handoff bookkeeping files (step-01-code-designer-rework1.json, step-01b-design-validator.json) -- docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md (DATA-DESIGNER's) does not appear in the diff at all, matching the handoff's claim that it was not touched and did not need rework (my prior gate had already found no defect in it).

2. Re-verified the exact attack named in my original FAIL, for all three callback handlers (SS4.6 now describes makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler, makeProfileStudentCallbackHandler, makeProfileExperienceCallbackHandler as one shared 7-step sequence, explicitly stated to apply to 'each' of the three -- confirmed the numbered steps 1-7 at lines 684-718 of the current file are written as a single shared discipline, not three separately-drifting descriptions that could diverge in an implementation):
   - Step 3: hasConsented/hasChapter read from flowUser, profile = getProfileByUserId(...).
   - Step 4: step = determineOnboardingStep(hasConsented, hasChapter, profile) (SS3.1) -- computed fresh from current DB state, before any write function is named.
   - Step 5 (the gate): write proceeds if and only if step.kind === 'profile-field' AND step.field matches the callback's claimed field; every other step.kind ('consent-needed', 'chapter-needed', 'ready') or a mismatched field is an explicit no-op -- no write function called at all.
   - Step 6: only past the gate, the matching write (markOptionalProfileFieldSkipped / writeRequiredProfileField) is called.
   Traced the concrete case by hand: a forged/stale `profile:skip:phone`-style callback_data arriving while consent_pd_at IS NULL. hasConsented is false (read directly off flowUser at step 3, not inferred from the callback). determineOnboardingStep's own stated rule (SS3.1's table, row 1: `!hasConsented` -> `{ kind: 'consent-needed' }`) means step 4 necessarily derives `{ kind: 'consent-needed' }`, unconditionally, regardless of which field the callback_data string names. Step 5's gate requires `step.kind === 'profile-field'`, which `'consent-needed'` never satisfies -- the AND-clause short-circuits false, the write is skipped, and the handler proceeds straight to step 7 (re-run advanceOnboarding, which will re-show the consent prompt). This holds identically for all three handlers because they share the same step 1-7 sequence and the same determineOnboardingStep call -- there is no per-handler branch that could diverge and skip the gate. The same trace applies verbatim to a stale-but-valid-looking callback arriving while hasChapter is false (step 4 derives 'chapter-needed', same gate failure) and to a callback naming a field that isn't the currently-derived one (e.g. an 'experience' callback tapped while the derived step names 'phone' -- step.field mismatch, same no-op). This is now a mechanism spelled out in the design's own text (step 4 computed BEFORE step 6's write is even named), not an asserted guarantee layered on top of an unconditional write, which was the exact defect my prior FAIL identified. S1's negative case ('a flow that writes a Profile row before consent is recorded') is now demonstrably closed for all three callback handlers, and the design is explicit and mechanical enough (per core-directives.md's weak-model-tolerance rule) that a limited-judgment implementer following SS4.6's numbered steps literally cannot reorder the write before the gate without visibly deviating from the stated sequence.

3. Zero-implementation-code check re-confirmed for the changed section: the code fence at lines ~660-678 (make*CallbackHandler signatures) is unchanged from the version that already passed this check -- still bare `export function ...(): ... { return async (ctx: Context): Promise<void> => { ... }; }` stub bodies, no real statements. The added 7-step sequence and the closing paragraph (lines 680-718) are prose outside any code fence -- no new code block was introduced by this rework, and no existing bare-signature block gained a body. No new design-system token referenced (this section still has no visual/CSS surface, matching SS9's existing vacuous-satisfaction statement, unchanged by this diff). Rework did not regress the zero-code check.

4. SS7's AC2 row re-checked against SS2.2's own derivation table. AC2 now reads 'completeness requires all six required columns non-null AND every optional field resolved (non-null OR marked skipped), exactly as SS2.2's derivation table states; skipping never counts against completeness because "explicitly skipped" is itself a resolved state, not a missing one.' Compared directly against SS2.2's determineNextProfileField rule table (step 3: 'All six required fields are non-null, and every optional field is either non-null or marked skipped' -> `{ kind: 'complete' }`) -- now word-for-word consistent, closing the MINOR finding. Also matches REQ-019-schema.md SS9's AC4 row, which was already accurate and untouched.

5. Re-confirmed nothing else changed: `git diff 0416a91 2dadd9f -- docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md` is empty (DATA-DESIGNER's schema doc genuinely untouched, as the handoff stated). No other section of REQ-019.md differs from the version I already passed everything-but-SS4.6/SS7 in (diff is scoped to exactly the SS4.6 rewrite and the SS7 AC2 sentence, confirmed by reading the full `git show 2dadd9f` diff, not a summary of it) -- SS0-SS3, SS4.1-SS4.5, SS5-SS6, SS8-SS9 are byte-identical to the version already verified, so no re-verification of those sections' own findings is needed; they were not touched and are not implicated in either finding this rework addressed.

Both findings from my prior FAIL are closed: the MAJOR S1 gap in SS4.6 (now an explicit derive-then-gate mechanism, verified for all three handlers and the consent-needed/chapter-needed/field-mismatch cases) and the MINOR SS7/SS2.2 inconsistency (now word-for-word consistent). No new finding introduced by this rework.
